work.title: Raindrops Keep Fallin’ on My Head
work.note: “Raindrops Keep Fallin’ on My Head” é uma canção de 1969, do filme Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid, sobre ficar feliz mesmo com a chuva. Na aula, o Rui e o Sam falam de um dia molhado: “It was raining hard.” A cena desta aula é original; não reproduz a obra.

facts.label: Passado contínuo
facts.sub: Use was/were + -ing para a ação em andamento e when + passado simples para a ação curta: I was walking when the rain started.

facts.label: Passado contínuo
facts.sub: Use was/were + -ing para uma ação em andamento: I was walking. We were waiting. It was raining. Use was com I, he, she e it; use were com you, we e they.

facts.label: Quando
facts.sub: Use when para a ação curta que aconteceu no meio: I was walking when the rain started. Depois de when, use o passado simples: started, came, drove.

pages.title: A bus stop in the rain · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy Wednesday afternoon in Houston. Water runs down the street. Sam stands under a small roof at a bus stop. His friend Rui arrives with wet clothes. Cars pass slowly in the rain. Sam laughs and asks a question.
“Rui! You’re all wet. What happened?” says Sam. “I was walking to the bus stop when the rain started.” says Rui. “Did you have an umbrella?” says Sam.
